summary: This is a Docker Compose configuration file that sets up a Joomla website with a PostgreSQL database. It defines two services: a Joomla web application container that runs on port 8080, and a PostgreSQL database container that Joomla depends on. Both containers use template variables (marked with %%) that get replaced with actual values when the file is deployed.

explanations.1: The %% syntax with name=kingsbridge%% is a template variable that will be replaced with an actual project name when this configuration is used.
explanations.7: restart: always means Docker will automatically restart this container if it crashes or the server reboots, ensuring your site stays up.
explanations.9: This maps port 8080 on your computer to port 80 inside the container, so you can access Joomla by visiting localhost:8080 in your browser.
explanations.11: JOOMLA_DB_HOST=joomladb tells Joomla where to find its database — 'joomladb' is the name of the database service defined later in this file.
explanations.13: JOOMLA_DB_USER=postgres sets the username that Joomla will use to log into the PostgreSQL database.
explanations.14: This template variable will be replaced with an actual password; using %% syntax instead of hardcoding keeps secrets out of version control.
explanations.18: pgsql tells Joomla it's connecting to a PostgreSQL database, not MySQL or another database type.
explanations.24: postgres:16.0-alpine uses a lightweight version of PostgreSQL (alpine) to save disk space and memory.
explanations.29: POSTGRES_DB=joomla_db creates an initial database named 'joomla_db' that Joomla will use to store its data.
explanations.31: POSTGRES_USER=postgres sets the username for the database administrator account.
explanations.33: This is the database password that matches the one Joomla uses (line 14) so the two services can authenticate with each other.
